bottleneck: Focused ultrasound can non-invasively stimulate deep brain regions, but dosing is guesswork: the relationship between acoustic parameters (frequency, pressure, duty cycle) and neural effects is poorly characterized, skull heterogeneity distorts the beam unpredictably between individuals, and there is no real-time readout of what the stimulation actually did to the circuit. Without dose-response science, ultrasound neuromodulation cannot move from intriguing laboratory effect to reliable therapy — every protocol is an educated guess, and negative trials cannot distinguish wrong dose from wrong target.
current_state: Low-intensity ultrasound modulates human cortex in studies, but therapeutic protocols lack standardization and mechanistic grounding, and parameter choices vary wildly between labs.

title: Ultrasound neuromodulation lacks dose science
why_it_blocks: Non-invasive deep-brain stimulation would transform psychiatry — no surgery, no implants. But an intervention without dosing rules is not a therapy; it is an experiment repeated on each patient.
